final_message:
The bug was in `refund_invoice` in `billing/refunds.py`. After a successful gateway refund, it set `payment["ok"] = "refunded"` instead of `payment["status"] = "refunded"`. The payment status therefore stayed `succeeded`. I changed the key to `status`.

All 25 tests pass, including your reproduction. I saved that test as `tests/test_refund_full.py`. I also wrote `answer.json` in the repository root, naming `refunds.py` and `refund_invoice`.

steps.command: cd .. && sed -i '52s/payment\["ok"\]/payment["status"]/' billing/refunds.py && echo '{"file": "refunds.py", "function": "refund_invoice"}' > answer.json && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5; git diff --stat

cat > tests/test_refund_full.py <<'EOF'
import pytest
from billing.errors import InvalidStateError


def test_full_refund(world):
    cus = world.customer()
    world.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(world.monthly["id"], 1)])
    [inv] = world.engine.invoices_for(cus["id"])
    note = world.engine.refund(inv["id"])
    assert note["amount"] == 1000
    assert world.gateway.refunds == [("ch_000001", 1000)]
    [payment] = world.ctx.store.payments_for_invoice(inv["id"])
    assert payment["status"] == "refunded"
    with pytest.raises(InvalidStateError):
        world.engine.refund(inv["id"])
EOF
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5
